QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_4

question.text: Ganga Infra AIF (a Category II scheme) has investible funds of INR 800 crore. The IC is considering a single cheque into Nirmal Power Ltd, a late-stage unlisted infrastructure SPV. What is the MAXIMUM amount the Manager may commit to Nirmal Power Ltd under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations' single-investee concentration norm applicable to Category II?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Comparison table (Table 3.1) in Chapter 3, the maximum investment in a particular investee company by a Category II AIF scheme cannot exceed 25% of the investible funds of the AIF scheme. 25% of INR 800 crore = INR 200 crore. The Trap: 10% is the Category III single-investee cap — this is a classic Cat II vs Cat III swap trap. 20% and 50% are fabricated distractors that sound plausible for a regulated concentration limit but do not appear in the AIF Regulations. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 25%/10% split across categories. XIX-E (Cat III Managers) will go deeper on the 10% Cat III cap. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) has a distinct 25%-per-issuer norm applicable to discretionary PMS — conceptually similar but under a different regulation. Manager's Pro-Tip: For co-investment deals that exceed the 25% cap, structure the excess as a parallel LP-level co-investment vehicle outside the AIF — but confirm that co-investment rights are explicitly reserved in the PPM and the LPA, otherwise the anchor LP will invoke MFN and drag all other LPs in.
